tasks.gr6-capacity-t4: Topic: Capacity and volume. Cover the meaning of capacity, metric units (millilitres and litres), conversion between ml and l, reading a measuring jug, and solving capacity problems in context. Ask Grade 6 learners to convert between ml and l, read measuring jugs, and solve practical capacity problems.
tasks.gr6-data-handling-t4: Topic: Data handling and statistics. Cover the mean, mode, median, and range of a data set, reading bar graphs and pie charts, and interpreting information from graphs. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate mean, mode, median, and range, and read and interpret different types of graphs.
tasks.gr6-mass-t4: Topic: Mass and weight. Cover units of mass (grams, kilograms, tonnes), converting between units, reading scales, and solving mass problems in context. Ask Grade 6 learners to convert between mass units, read mass from scales, and solve practical mass problems.
tasks.gr6-problem-solving-t4: Topic: Multi-step problem solving. Cover reading word problems carefully, identifying key information, planning solution steps, performing calculations, and checking answers. Ask Grade 6 learners to solve multi-step word problems involving all four operations, fractions, and measurement in real-world contexts.
tasks.gr6-time-t4: Topic: Time. Cover reading analogue and digital clocks, 12-hour and 24-hour time formats, converting between them, and calculating elapsed time and duration. Ask Grade 6 learners to read clocks, convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time, and calculate time differences.
tasks.gr6-multiply-3digit-t4: Topic: Multiplying whole numbers by 3-digit numbers (4-digit by 3-digit). Cover estimating (how the rounding changes the estimate), long multiplication with three partial products (the hundreds, tens and ones digits, a 0 digit gives no partial product), and problems with money and rates. Write numbers with a space between groups of three digits (471 096) and rand as R225 000. Ask Grade 6 learners to estimate and calculate with whole-number answers.
tasks.gr6-divide-3digit-t4: Topic: Dividing whole numbers by 3-digit numbers (4-digit by 3-digit). Cover estimating, a clue board of multiples of the divisor, long division by multiplying and subtracting (3 484 / 132 = 26 remainder 52), exact divisions, checking by multiplying, and remainders in problems with money, pallets and packets. Write numbers with a space between groups of three digits. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate with a remainder written as, for example, 26 remainder 52.
tasks.gr6-probability-t4: Topic: Probability experiments. Cover listing the possible outcomes of tossing a coin (heads or tails), rolling a die (1 to 6) and spinning a spinner with equal sections (one outcome for each different colour or number), recording trials with tally marks (groups of five), counting and comparing frequencies (most often, least often, how many more, a missing frequency that makes the total), up to 50 trials, and collating the results of groups. Do not write probabilities as fractions or use the words chance or likely; Grade 6 counts and compares frequencies only. Ask Grade 6 learners to read tables and tallies and calculate with whole numbers.
tasks.gr6-position-movement-t4: Topic: Position and movement on an alpha-numeric grid. Cover grid references with the column letter first and the row number second (D4), reading letters across the top and numbers down the side (rows counted from the top), giving directions between squares (3 squares right, then 2 squares down), following a list of moves, counting the squares walked, and compass directions when north is at the top of the map (north up, south down, east right, west left). Describe the grid in the question because there is no picture. Ask Grade 6 learners to give a grid reference, follow directions or give directions.
tasks.gr6-enlargements-t4: Topic: Enlargements and reductions of triangles and quadrilaterals. Cover multiplying every side by the same whole number to enlarge (doubling, tripling) and dividing every side by the same number to reduce (halving), what changes (size, side lengths, perimeter, area) and what stays the same (shape, angles), the perimeter and area of enlarged and reduced rectangles (doubling both sides makes the area 4 times as big), and that changing only one pair of opposite sides changes the shape. Use whole-number lengths in cm. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate side lengths, perimeters and areas.
